sources.entry: PiGallery 2 - Directory-first photo gallery website, with a rich UI, optimised for running on low resource servers. (Source Code) MIT Docker/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: PiGallery2 is a fast, directory-first photo gallery website designed to run on low-resource servers such as Raspberry Pi.
summary.what_it_does: PiGallery2 serves a web photo gallery that shows your existing folder structure as it is, rather than building an album database. The README says it is simple to set up: you point it at your photos and it is ready to use. It is described as read-only, meaning the photo folder is never modified. It is optimized for low-end hardware, especially Raspberry Pi. The README names Docker as the recommended way to run it and says a native Node.js installation is possible but unsupported. Documentation covers an FAQ, configuration guide, user rights, and a contribution guide. A live demo is linked, with a first-load delay of up to 60 seconds while the server boots.
use_cases: browse photos by folder on a Raspberry Pi
view a home photo library over the web
read-only photo sharing from a server
lightweight alternative to heavy photo management apps
how_to_run: Install with Docker (recommended; the README section has no commands listed)
Native Node.js installation is possible but unsupported; see the documentation for details
notable: Directory-first: shows the folder structure of your photos as it is
Read-only: the photo folder is never modified
Optimized for low-resource servers and Raspberry Pi
caveats: Native installation is not officially supported; Docker is the recommended route
Live demo may take up to 60 seconds to respond on first load while the server boots
